newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Pro-independence mood growing in Taiwan - poll.
newsitem.headline: Pro-independence mood growing in Taiwan - poll.

text.p: Independence from China is gaining more support among Taiwan people, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday after two years in which the country's relations with Beijing have turned acrimonious.
The poll, conducted by the mass-circulation United Daily News, showed that 34 percent of 1,014 respondents supported full independence from China, up from 24 percent in February 1995.

The number advocating independence was just three percent under the 37 percent supporting reunification with the mainland, according to the poll, conducted over two days this week. The remainder had no comment.
In the poll two years ago, the number supporting reunification was 42 percent.
The newspaper said the growth of the pro-independence sentiment was spurred by China's military intimidation against Taiwan, but did not elaborate.

Beijing staged a series of war games, including four missile tests off Taiwan, between August 1995 and March 1996 to try to intimidate the island over what it perceived as a growing trend toward independence.
It suspended semi-official talks with Taiwan shortly after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui visited the United States in June 1995 in a trip it interpreted as an attempt to promote independence.
China and Taiwan split after a civil war in 1949, but Beijing still regards the island as an inseparable part of the mainland subject to eventual unification.
China has threatened to attack Taiwan if it declares independence.
